```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(polymarketR)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
```

Idea: Need to compile all (or many) markets related to 2024 US Elections.

Each event contains 1 or more markets. So, we search for all events and then can find all markets from there.

Each event has a unique "slug" (or text identifier) and id. Each event also contains multiple tags (or keywords that are associated with it).

PolymarketR lets us search for events based on text and slugs. We could search across many "text terms", but searching by slugs may give us a more comprehensive portion of the event landscape. 

My current idea: 
1.) Use basic text queries to search for events with PolymarketR
2.) From those events, find specific, relevant associated tags
3.) Use given tags (alongside election dates, etc.) via Polymarket Gamma API to compile list of events that fall under given tags
4.) Use PolymarketR to identify all markets etc. from given events

```{r}
event_slugs <- search_events("2024 US election")

event_slugs
```
```{r}
sample_event <- get_event_by_slug("presidential-election-winner-2024")
```

```{r}
sample_event$tags[[1]]
```
```{r}
get_events_by_tag <- function(tag_id) {
  events_url <- str_c("https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?tag_id=",
                    tag_id,
                    "&closed=true&related_tags=true&end_date_min=2024-11-01&end_date_max=2025-01-31")

  pulled_events <- GET(url = events_url)

  events <- fromJSON(
    content(pulled_events, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
  )
  
  return(events)
}

tag_ids <- c("1101", "1102", "185", "589", "57", "24")

event_datasets <- map(tag_ids, get_events_by_tag)
events_final <- list_rbind(event_datasets) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

events_final
